title: Helm Financial - MSA/DPA Acceptance & SLA Readout
summary: Redwood and Helm ran through final acceptance of MSA/DPA redlines, clarified SLA targets, and aligned on an initial pilot procurement path. Key open items: KMS/HSM language, egress+egress fee cap, audit log retention, and formal legal-to-legal handoff for two DPA clauses. Price approval path confirmed (finance signoff required), pilot start targeted early May.
topics: Pricing approval cadence and PO path
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Devon Chen, Liam O'Neill - Redwood; Priya Nair, Marcus Reed, Olivia Park, Samir Patel - Helm Financial

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Ava on the account team, Devon is our SE, Liam's on CSM and we'll walk through the MSA/DPA updates and the SLA readout.

[00:18] Priya Nair: Hi Ava, thanks. We're here because procurement wants a final readout before finance signs the PO, and legal has a couple outstanding DPA items.

[00:28] Olivia Park: Yep, I circulated the redlines. There were two DPA points we haven't accepted yet — the subprocessor clause and the audit retention point.

[00:40] Devon Chen: Great, we'll tackle those. Quick note, some of the product names in the doc may have formatting errors — e.g. Redwood Dedicate appears in the copy but the platform offering is Redwood Dedicated, so small editorials aside.

[00:52] Marcus Reed: Also want to flag encryption: we need explicit KMS/HSM mentions and key ownership language. We run a BYOK model in some pilots, so clarity on who holds keys and where is critical.

[01:10] Liam O'Neill: Understood; we've done private deployments with customer-managed KMS. We can add a standard clause stating customer retains key ownership and Redwood will support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM via bring-your-own-key workflows).

[01:35] Samir Patel: Can you confirm whether audit logs are accessible for 12 months? The DPA draft says 6 months but security asked for 12 for incident forensics.

[01:48] Ava Martinez: The default offering is 6 months retention on audit logs in hosted, but for dedicated and private we can extend retention to 12 months as an add-on in the contract. That would be part of the SOW or an addendum.

[02:05] Olivia Park: Okay we need that spelled out in the DPA — retention period by deployment type. Also, can we confirm data residency controls? Helm has EU customer data that must remain in EU regions.

[02:20] Devon Chen: Yes — routing policies can pin requests to region-specific clusters. For hosted we can guarantee processing in eu-west-1 or equivalent region; for private deployments it's customer-controlled. We'll add region pinning language.

[02:36] Priya Nair: On pricing, finance wants an estimate for committed spend vs on-demand. We discussed a pilot that would be a 3-month reserved capacity with a lower per-token rate. Is that still feasible?

[02:49] Ava Martinez: Absolutely. We proposed a pilot reserved pool — it's essentially a small Dedicated reservation for the pilot, three months, convertible to longer-term reserved capacity. We can lock per-token pricing for the pilot term.

[03:05] Marcus Reed: Are there egress fees if we export embeddings or logs for internal tools? We want to avoid unpredictable egress charges.

[03:15] Liam O'Neill: Egress is typically billed per GB for logs and exports, but for pilots we can cap egress charges or include a nominal cap in the PO so you don't get surprises.

[03:30] Olivia Park: We need a clear cap in the MSA or a price schedule. Also, the contractual SLA target — our operations team wants a 99.9% availability SLA with defined crediting. The draft MSA has 99.5.

[03:45] Devon Chen: 99.9 does change the operational profile. For Dedicated we can commit to 99.9 with defined maintenance windows and scheduled patching. For hosted, 99.5 is our standard. We can offer 99.9 as a premium SLA tied to Dedicated or private.

[04:05] Priya Nair: Helm prefers the higher SLA, even if it's pricier. But we need the crediting formula spelled out and an escalation path.

[04:15] Ava Martinez: We'll include an SLA appendix with tech metrics: uptime calculation, exclusion windows, service credits formula (x% credit per y minutes under threshold), and a defined legal escalation ladder.

[04:30] Samir Patel: Back to DPA: the subprocessor list — you noted it could change. We need an obligation to notify and a 30-day objection window.

[04:40] Devon Chen: Standard approach is notification of changes with an ability to object within 30 days. For subprocessors used in critical data flows we can add a requirement to use SOC2-compliant subprocessors only.

[04:55] Olivia Park: Also, Helms legal asked that data deletion upon termination be certified. We want a deletion certificate or attestation.

[05:05] Ava Martinez: We can provide a deletion attestation and a description of deletion processes for each deployment type. For private/on-prem we outline customer responsibilities plus Redwood's actions on our managed control plane.

[05:20] Marcus Reed: About the audit rights — Helms security prefers on-site audits are off the table, but remote audits and third-party reports (SOC2 Type II) suffice. Is that acceptable?

[05:33] Olivia Park: We want the right to request an independent third-party assessment if there's a serious incident.

[05:40] Devon Chen: That's reasonable — we can commit to providing SOC2 reports and allow an independent assessment under strict confidentiality for cause. We'll add a process for request, scope, and cost allocation.

[05:55] Priya Nair: Good. On procurement timing: if legal and finance sign off, leadership wants to start pilot 2026-05-04. Is that timeline doable?

[06:05] Liam O'Neill: Yes, it's reasonable. Onboarding for a small Dedicated pilot typically takes 3-6 weeks from PO and payment depending on VPC/network setup.

[06:18] Samir Patel: Network wise, we'll require IP allowlist, VPC peering or PrivateLink, and support for static egress IPs. Can Redwood provide static egress?

[06:30] Devon Chen: For Dedicated and private deployments we can provision static egress IPs. For hosted, there are options like customer gateway and VPC egress proxies; static egress can be part of the premium network setup.

[06:45] Priya Nair: Liability cap — Helm's legal wants 3x fees or $10M whichever is lower. The draft MSA has a flat cap of $1M.

[06:56] Olivia Park: Right, we need to negotiate that.

[07:04] Ava Martinez: We can propose a middle ground: 3x fees for pilot and up to $5M for enterprise rollout, with carve-outs for gross negligence or willful misconduct. We'll mark that as negotiable with legal-to-legal.

[07:20] Priya Nair: OK. Can you confirm Redwood's compliance posture — SOC2, ISO, FedRAMP roadmap? 

[07:29] Devon Chen: Current: SOC2 Type II in place; ISO 27001 in process; FedRAMP is on the roadmap but not committed date. We'll share the latest attestation and a public compliance page.

[07:43] Marcus Reed: We need a timeline for ISO if it's a gating criteria.

[07:48] Ava Martinez: I'll follow up with a general timeline estimate; can't commit legally here but will share current status and expected cadence.

[07:58] Olivia Park: Back to price approval: who signs in Redwood for discounts? Finance needs a written pricing approval path.

[08:06] Ava Martinez: I can send the approved pricing schedule and the AE-approved discount matrix. Final approval for deviations sits with our pricing committee (cc: sales ops). I'll include approver contacts.

[08:20] Priya Nair: Next — SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Helm uses Okta. We need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning documented.

[08:31] Devon Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM; we'll provide the SSO integration guide and a small implementation checklist.

[08:45] Samir Patel: Service account permissions — we want RBAC so our teams only see their token usage and logs.

[08:53] Liam O'Neill: RBAC is available in the Console; we'll map roles during onboarding and document admin/readonly roles.

[09:05] Olivia Park: Can you confirm data encryption in transit and at rest? The DPA wants TLS 1.2+ in transit, and AES-256 at rest with customer key option.

[09:16] Devon Chen: Confirmed: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest; BYOK supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted also supports KMS integrations for key control.

[09:28] Priya Nair: Excellent. There's a minor wording request: include an exception process for legal redline items that require multi-stakeholder signoff, so procurement knows the expected review duration.

[09:39] Ava Martinez: We'll add a legal-to-legal SLA for redline turnaround: 7 business days for initial review, 15 for complex redlines. That will be in the MSA negotiation appendix.

[09:53] Olivia Park: On breach notification: Helm requires 72 hours maximum and a runbook. The DPA currently lists 5 business days.

[10:03] Marcus Reed: 72 hours is important for regulatory reporting.

[10:08] Devon Chen: We can agree to 72 hours for initial notification and provide a post-incident report within 30 days. Add to DPA.

[10:20] Priya Nair: Great. A few quick procurement items: PO format, tax residency, and invoicing frequency (monthly vs quarterly). Can finance get a sample invoice?

[10:30] Ava Martinez: Yes — we'll send a billing template and confirm invoicing cadence options. We typically support monthly or quarterly invoicing.

[10:42] Olivia Park: On subprocessors, will you publish an up-to-date list with compliance attestations?

[10:49] Devon Chen: Yes, we maintain a subprocessor page and can provide attestations and SOC reports on request.

[11:00] Priya Nair: Anything on export controls? Helm operates in regulated finance sectors; need assurance there are controls on model access.

[11:08] Ava Martinez: We can add export control language and restrict model weights export; also put in a clause about no model custody — models are provided as a service and not redistributable.

[11:20] Samir Patel: Network latency and performance — can you commit to p95 latency targets for the pilot? We want estimates for 128-token generation at p95.

[11:30] Devon Chen: We'll run a baseline benchmark with your prompt set. Typical p95 for similar workloads on Dedicated is ~120-200ms for 128-token generation depending on model family. We'll provide an appendix with benchmark results and target SLOs.

[11:50] Olivia Park: So we do a benchmark then attach to SOW?

[11:55] Liam O'Neill: Correct — benchmark results for your prompt set can be attached to the SOW and used as acceptance criteria for pilot success.

[12:04] Priya Nair: Good. Let's outline next steps now so procurement has a clear path.

[12:10] Ava Martinez: Recap and next steps — we'll: 1) send a redlined MSA with the agreed KMS, retention, and SLA appendices; 2) share SOC2 report and subprocessor attestations; 3) provide pricing schedule and pilot PO template; 4) schedule legal-to-legal for outstanding liability and DPA clauses; 5) plan benchmark with Samir for week of 2026-04-13.

[12:40] Olivia Park: For the legal-to-legal call, we'll need counsel available April 6 or 7, do those dates work?

[12:48] Ava Martinez: I can do April 7, I'll loop in our legal.

[12:55] Priya Nair: Finance will push for approval once they have the signed MSA and pricing.

[13:02] Samir Patel: We'll prepare network access info and send a sample prompt set for benchmarking.

[13:10] Liam O'Neill: We'll schedule the benchmark kickoff and share the SOW template with acceptance criteria.

[13:20] Ava Martinez: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the package by Friday. If legal wants an earlier draft, we can do an interim send tomorrow.

[13:32] Priya Nair: Please do. That helps expedite.

[13:40] Olivia Park: One last question — contract signature authority. Helm signs POs centrally; who's the Redwood signer?

[13:48] Ava Martinez: Our standard is VP of Revenue or General Counsel depending on the contract size; I'll include the approver in the pricing doc.

[13:58] Meeting close: agreed next steps, legal-to-legal on April 7, pilot benchmark week of April 13, target pilot start May 4.

Notes: transcription had occasional minor speaker attribution errors; some technical terms transcribed as KV cache -> K V cache and Redwood Dedicated showed as Redwood Dedicate in the circulated draft.
